title.narrative: West Africa Regional Electricity Market Program (WA-REMP) MPA Phase 1 - Mauritania Transmission Corridor Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to scale up renewable energy deployment, increase access to electricity, and expand Mauritania's electricity export capacity.

The proposed operation, Mauritania Transmission Corridor, is part of Phase 1 of the WA-REMP MPA. It will include critical national level investments to support the reinforcement of the national grid for increased regional trade, and enable faster deployment of renewable energy as well as expansion of energy access in underserved areas. West Africa Regional Electricity Market Program (WA-REMP) is a Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA) operation that aims at helping West African countries fully exploit regional power system integration to advance on energy transition and reach energy security, all being pre-conditions to expand electricity access in the region. WA-REMP marks the next phase of the World Bank's engagement in regional power system integration in West Africa, which spans fifteen years and has made the Bank the primary partner for countries and regional agencies in the establishment of the West African Power Pool (WAPP) market. While completing physical infrastructures remains important, focus must shift towards lifting remaining barriers to a functional market, such as reducing WAPP market risks, ensuring that countries cooperate to develop an open and competitive regional market, addressing infrastructure gaps, and ultimately improving the climate for private investment, especially in renewable energy generation. To this end, WA-REMP establishes a new, systematic Bank approach to regional energy sector engagement in West Africa.
